Q: What is feedback on my SQL data modelling? What could I do better? How appropriate are my cardinalities? A:

Good use of XT generalization, that's right since File/Directory/Shortcut are mutually exclusive types.

One fix from my perspective is cardinality is backwards. You have Directory=1,1 and FSO=0,N - should be flipped: Directory=0,N (a directory holds 0 to N objects), FSO=1,1 (each object belongs to exactly one directory). Consider 0,1 instead of 1,1 on the File System Object side if you want a root directory to exist.

There is interesting read on github do have a look:

https://github.com/laowantong/mocodo/blob/master/README.md

Q: GCC accepts call to overloaded member function template while Clang rejects A:

The program is ill-formed as explained below. In C++23 the relevant rules are in basic.scope.scope:

Two function templates have corresponding signatures if their template-parameter-lists have the same length, their corresponding template-parameters are equivalent, they have equivalent non-object-parameter-type-lists and return types (if any), and, if both are non-static members, they have corresponding object parameters. Two declarations correspond if they (re)introduce the same name, both declare constructors, or both declare destructors, unless

  • Two function or function template declarations declare corresponding overloads if
    • both declare functions with the same non-object-parameter-type-list,¹⁴ equivalent ([temp.over.link]) trailing requires-clauses (if any, except as specified in [temp.friend]), and, if both are non-static members, they have corresponding object parameters, or
    • both declare function templates with corresponding signatures and equivalent template-heads and trailing requires-clauses (if any).

Since the implicit object parameters of these two non-static member function templates are same( which is S&), so these two declarations do correspond and the program is ill-formed.

Q: Debugging a GNOME Shell layout collapse: how a 4,294,967,296 px preferred height collapsed St.ScrollView to 1 px A:

Observed Facts & Clutter Allocation Behavior

The failure occurs when an unconstrained preferred size query near the 2^32 boundary breaks proportional layout allocation.

1. Input Parameter -1 (for_width)

In get_preferred_height(-1), -1 is the for_width input parameter representing an unconstrained query (clutter_actor_get_preferred_height). An unconstrained or invalid preferred size entered layout calculations when intermediate containers lacked explicit minimum dimensions or had conflicting alignment flags (x_align/y_align).

2. Clutter Allocation Clamping to min_height = 1px

In Clutter (clutter_actor_allocate), allocation box heights are clamped to minimum bounds: allocated_height = max(min_height, calculated_space). StScrollView has a minimum preferred height of minH = 1px (its baseline padding/border constraint). When parent ClutterBoxLayout attempted to distribute available height across siblings with an astronomical request (4,294,967,296 px), remaining space became zero or negative. Clutter clamped the child allocation box to its declared minimum size — exactly 1px.

3. gfloat Precision at 2^32

In Clutter (clutter/clutter-box-layout.c), layout size calculations use gfloat (32-bit IEEE 754 float). Near 2^32, float32 precision step is 256:

  • 2^32 = 4,294,967,296
  • 2^32 - 256 = 4,294,967,040 The logged values (4,294,967,296 and 4,294,967,040) match representable gfloat float32 numbers near the 2^32 limit.

Solution

  1. Diagnostic Workaround: To verify size constraint sensitivity during debugging: 
    grid.set_size(200, 300); // Diagnostic check
  2. Adaptive Production Solution:
    • Establish a single geometry owner (manage sizing in JS via Clutter actor flags).
    • Remove conflicting x_align and y_align parameters on intermediate child wrappers.
    • Use x_expand: true and y_expand: true so the parent layout manager handles dynamic resizing.
- const grid = new St.Widget({ 
-     x_align: Clutter.ActorAlign.CENTER, 
-     y_align: Clutter.ActorAlign.FILL 
- });
- grid.queue_relayout();
+ const grid = new St.Widget({
+     style_class: 'app-grid',
+     x_expand: true,
+     y_expand: true,
+ });

For full investigation logs and test scripts, see the Pasynkov Debugging Cookbook case investigation.

Q: Reverse authentication by password for the root user of MariaDB to do admin tasks via phpMyAdmin A:

The error is a syntax mistake. MariaDB 10.4+ uses IDENTIFIED VIA … USING PASSWORD() rather than IDENTIFIED WITH … BY.

Try this:

ALTER USER 'root'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED VIA mysql_native_password USING PASSWORD('password');

Starting with version 10.4, MariaDB defaults root@localhost to the unix_socket plugin. This matches the OS user and blocks TCP connections from tools like phpMyAdmin that run as www-data. Using the VIA syntax replaces that plugin with password auth.

But if you want to keep passwordless login at the terminal, I'd use both methods instead:

ALTER USER 'root'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED VIA unix_socket OR mysql_native_password USING PASSWORD('password');

This lets you connect as root without a password from the command line while still accepting a password from phpMyAdmin.

Q: Does g_form.onUserChangeValue work with unchecking checkbox? A:

I believe you're experiencing where the checkbox was initially loaded as unchecked. I've noticed the function won't trigger a call if the original value loaded is being returned-to. It seems to happen to the field types I've tried.
